benchmark: AstraDJ local multi-room Lounge acceptance and performance

methodology.queueWorkload: 3 rooms concurrently; 50 sockets per room; 1 serialized queue additions per second per room for 10 seconds; operations start at the configured interval and are flushed before report.
methodology.warmup: No synthetic mutation warm-up is included; join and schema index initialization occur before measurement.
methodology.trace: Each queue add carries a UUID correlation ID. Server command receipt and monotonic processing duration are captured in the gateway; the durable QueueEvent carries the correlation ID and receipt wall timestamp; each broadcast envelope already carries server wall-clock ts.
methodology.clockMethod: All API processes and Socket.IO clients run on one host and use the same OS wall clock; server/client wall timestamps are compared directly (no inter-host offset subtraction), with 1 ms clock-resolution allowance. No remote-host clock synchronization or deployment network behavior is established.
methodology.rateLimitHandling: The benchmark uses a unique disposable database. To collect more than five segue samples per room despite the production limit of 10 playback actions/user/minute, the benchmark clears only the disposable database rate-limit counters before segue sample 16. Rate-limit throughput is not measured by this workload.
methodology.clientApplyAndRender: Socket.IO driver applies the received queue snapshot to an in-memory client state and records a setImmediate render-callback proxy. It is not React/DOM/browser rendering and is not treated as actual rendered UI evidence.
methodology.percentiles: Nearest-rank p50/p95/p99 (ceil(p*n), 1-based); per-metric sample count shown. Three rooms aggregate for queue latency, with room-level breakdown.
methodology.chatAndReconnect: One unique persisted chat message per room delivered to every currently joined socket; disconnect a listener, send a second message, reconnect/join, and verify authoritative queue snapshot plus history recovery.
methodology.clientSourceAddresses: Each room uses a distinct loopback source address (127.0.0.1 onward) so its 50 initial sockets remain below the shared per-IP connection-attempt limit; this does not model a single-NAT 150-client burst.
methodology.lifecycle: Host end command, durable ended status, and end notification count observed per room.

prdTargets.concurrentRoomDescription: handful; local acceptance uses the configured room count

queueSyncDrift.boundary: Client in-memory state/render-callback proxy; not browser DOM rendering.

webSocketFanout.boundary: Server handler receipt to final Socket.IO client receipt on one host.

segue.disposition: Service/socket proxy only; no real media clock or browser render measurement. P95 target remains unverified even if the proxy is below 3000 ms.

prdDisposition.queueSyncDrift: Local simulated-client state/render-callback proxy only; not a production or browser-rendered acceptance result.
prdDisposition.webSocketFanout: Estimated from instrumented server receipt and envelope broadcast time plus per-client clock offset correction; local shared-host clock. Production network fan-out remains unverified.
prdDisposition.roomCapacity: Exercised at PRD design capacity in each local room; not production capacity proof.
prdDisposition.multipleRooms: 3 rooms exercised concurrently across two app processes against one local MongoDB instance.
prdDisposition.segue: Measured separately from queue event fan-out and remains unverified at the true outro-entry-to-browser-rendered boundary.
